scope: Development scratch pilots, not formal acceptance; APG is the project BPTT implementation.
question: Can differentiable actor optimization learn the shared goal-reaching task under the same forward conditions as the batch64 PPO candidate?
shared: Seed 0; depth Actor GRU192; goal/rotation/time observation; first-principles cf21B_500 500Hz, acceleration target heading 10Hz; 64 worlds x horizon32; goal-reaching reward gamma1; identical procedural curriculum and 2211840 interactions; same checkpoint/evaluation schedules and cases.

algorithm_differences.apg: Exact rematerialized action-to-physics actor gradient with temporal incoming-state gradient decay alpha=0.916290731874155; actor lr .0003; no critic objective; deterministic rollout.
algorithm_differences.shac: Same differentiable actor path, terminal target-critic input gradient enabled with weight1; state-only critic lr .001, 4 fit epochs, target old-weight .995, lambda .95; deterministic rollout.
algorithm_differences.ppo: Score-function on-policy Gaussian objective, privileged training-only critic lr .0005; actor lr .0002; entropy .005; other PPO settings unchanged.

decision: Compare complete fixed-case reports and episode progress at equal interactions. Screen improvements are provisional; convergence still requires three seeds, full checks, continued learning and fresh frozen cohorts. Persistent collisions with little avoidance under both differentiable methods would challenge the sufficiency of the current short-horizon differentiable objective; it would not prove all BPTT/SHAC settings fail.
data: No pretrained parameters, teacher actions or benchmark episodes used in learning; all pilot test cohorts are development information.
